speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to assess this newborn, so could you please describe the specific findings on physical examination and any relevant history provided?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Since there was no prenatal care, did the mother have any known infections like syphilis, HIV, or hepatitis B during her pregnancy? Also, have you noticed any specific rashes, respiratory distress, or feeding difficulties in the newborn since delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of a continuous heart murmur, cloudy lenses (cataracts), and hearing loss is highly suggestive of Congenital Rubella Syndrome. Did the mother report having a rash or fever during the first trimester of her pregnancy?

REQUEST TEST: Rubella_IgM

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Rubella IgM confirms acute infection, which, combined with the classic triad of cataracts, hearing loss, and cardiac defects (likely a patent ductus arteriosus causing the continuous murmur), is diagnostic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome
